channel.title: ePowerAI
channel.description: Project-based courses from Linear Algebra and Optimization through RL, Robot Learning, Physical AI, Generative Models, Probability & Statistics, and Advanced Optimization — short concepts paired with hands-on builds.

item.title: Start Here: Python and the Math the Labs Use
item.description: Your first step in the Guided Foundations Path: run a browser Python cell, read its output and a traceback, use variables, lists, loops, if/else and functions, build numpy arrays, and read a sum, an average, an area under a curve, and a slope.

item.title: Week 1: Vectors and Linear Combinations
item.description: Two arrows in the plane. Drag them to see the parallelogram of addition and the scalar the dot product reports.

item.title: Week 2: Linear Transformations and Matrices
item.description: A unit grid deforms under a 2 by 2 matrix. The signed area of the unit square is the determinant, and matrix multiplication is composition.

item.title: Week 3: Elimination and LU Factorization
item.description: Solve linear systems by Gaussian elimination, see elimination as matrix multiplication, and factor A = LU.

item.title: Week 4: Determinants
item.description: Learn the defining properties of the determinant, compute it by cofactor expansion, and use it to test invertibility and measure volume.

item.title: Week 5: Vector Spaces, Independence, and Basis
item.description: Test vector sets for linear independence, and learn how a basis pins down the dimension of a vector space.

item.title: Week 6: The Four Fundamental Subspaces
item.description: Meet the column space, null space, row space, and left null space of a matrix, and the rank-nullity formula that ties their dimensions together.

item.title: Week 7: Orthogonality and Projections
item.description: Project a vector onto a line or a subspace, and build the projection matrix that does it automatically.

item.title: Week 8: Least Squares and QR
item.description: Fit lines to noisy data with least squares, build orthonormal bases with Gram-Schmidt, and factor A = QR.

item.title: Week 9: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
item.description: Find the directions a matrix only stretches, not rotates — eigenvalues and eigenvectors via the characteristic equation.

item.title: Week 10: Diagonalization and Markov Matrices
item.description: Diagonalize a matrix to compute powers efficiently, and use eigenvalues to find the steady state of a Markov chain.

item.title: Week 11: Differential Equations
item.description: Solve systems of linear differential equations using eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and read off stability from their signs.

item.title: Week 12: Symmetric and Positive Definite Matrices
item.description: Meet the spectral theorem for symmetric matrices, and learn three equivalent tests for positive definiteness.

item.title: Week 13: The SVD and Complex Matrices
item.description: Generalize eigendecomposition to any matrix with the singular value decomposition, and meet the complex analogues of symmetric and orthogonal matrices.

item.title: Week 14: The Fourier Matrix, FFT, and PCA
item.description: Meet the Fourier matrix and the FFT that makes it fast, then close the course with PCA — variance-maximizing directions found via the SVD.

item.title: Week 1: Optimization for Learning
item.description: Formulate empirical risk minimization, define loss surfaces, and implement gradient descent on a simple quadratic using multivariable calculus.

item.title: Week 2: Convex Sets and Functions
item.description: Recognize convex sets and functions, and understand why a local minimum of a convex function is automatically global.

item.title: Week 3: Gradient Descent Theory
item.description: Understand why GD converges: L-smoothness, convexity, and step-size rules that guarantee monotonic progress.

item.title: Week 4: Least Squares and Conditioning
item.description: Solve least squares iteratively with GD and see how the condition number of the design matrix controls convergence speed.

item.title: Week 5: Classification Losses
item.description: Differentiate logistic, softmax, and cross-entropy losses, and see why convexity extends from regression to classification.

item.title: Week 6: Stochastic Gradient Descent
item.description: Replace full-batch gradients with mini-batch estimates, trade noise for speed, and tune learning rates under stochasticity.

item.title: Week 7: Momentum and Acceleration
item.description: Add velocity to gradient steps with heavy-ball momentum and see why Nesterov acceleration improves convergence on convex problems.

item.title: Week 8: Adaptive First-Order Methods
item.description: Let each parameter learn at its own rate with AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam, the methods that train deep neural networks.

item.title: Week 9: Practical Training Dynamics
item.description: Diagnose training runs with learning rate schedules, warmup, gradient clipping, and the art of reading loss curves.

item.title: Week 10: Nonsmooth and Composite Objectives
item.description: Handle ReLU, L1, and other nondifferentiable losses with subgradients, and see how early stopping acts as implicit regularization.

item.title: Week 11: Constraints: Projections and Penalties
item.description: Enforce constraints with projected gradient descent and soft penalties, and glimpse Lagrange multipliers as constraint pricing.

item.title: Week 12: Duality for Practitioners
item.description: Build the Lagrangian dual, state weak and strong duality, and compute the soft-margin SVM dual as a concrete ML example.

item.title: Week 13: Nonconvex Deep Learning
item.description: Cross from convex land into the reality of deep net training: saddles, overparameterization, initialization, and normalization.

item.title: Week 14: Capstone — Theory Meets Training
item.description: Diagnose a full training pipeline, choose methods and learning rates from first principles, and map course tools onto RL and generative model training.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning: Agents, Rewards, and MDPs
item.description: Meet the reinforcement-learning loop in plain language — an agent acts, the world answers with a reward and a next state — and learn the five ingredients that make the problem solvable.

item.title: Bandits: Exploration, Exploitation, and Regret
item.description: The simplest reinforcement-learning problem: a row of slot machines, no states, and one unavoidable trade-off. Learn why always choosing the current best is not enough — and how to measure the reward that exploring costs you.

item.title: Returns, Value, and the Bellman Equation
item.description: Turn a stream of rewards into a single number: discounting, the return, value functions, and the one recursive equation that makes infinite-horizon problems solvable.

item.title: Bandits: UCB1 and Thompson Sampling
item.description: Two principled answers to the exploration problem: trust the optimistic edge of what you know (UCB1), or sample from what you believe (Thompson sampling). Both explore automatically, with no rate to tune.

item.title: Week 1: Reinforcement Learning Problem Formulation
item.description: Formalize sequential decision making as Markov Decision Processes, derive value functions and the Bellman equations, and understand the reward hypothesis and its limits.

item.title: Week 2: Multi-Armed Bandits
item.description: Formalize the exploration-exploitation trade-off as a multi-armed bandit problem, derive the Lai-Robbins lower bound, and implement UCB1 and Thompson Sampling from first principles.

item.title: Week 3: Dynamic Programming for Finite MDPs
item.description: Master policy evaluation, policy iteration, and value iteration for finite MDPs. Understand the contraction mapping property that guarantees DP convergence, and trace the precise mappings from DP to Q-learning, actor-critic, and RLHF.

item.title: Week 4: Monte Carlo and Temporal-Difference Learning
item.description: Master Monte Carlo and Temporal-Difference methods for learning value functions from experience. Understand the bias-variance tradeoff that defines every modern deep RL algorithm, from SARSA and Q-learning to PPO and DQN.

item.title: Week 5: Function Approximation in Reinforcement Learning
item.description: How function approximation breaks tabular RL convergence — the MSVE objective, the deadly triad mechanism, Baird's counterexample, overestimation bias, and the neural network instabilities that DQN's target networks fix.

item.title: Week 6: Deep Q-Learning and Variants
item.description: How DQN stabilizes deep RL with experience replay, target networks, and reward clipping, plus Double DQN, Dueling, Prioritized Replay, Distributional RL, and Rainbow.

item.title: Week 7: Policy Gradient and Actor–Critic Methods
item.description: Derive the policy gradient theorem from first principles, build REINFORCE to actor-critic, develop GAE, and connect PPO to RLHF — the algorithmic backbone of modern language model alignment.

item.title: Week 8: Modern Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
item.description: Explore the off-policy actor-critic family — DDPG, TD3, and SAC — from deterministic policy gradients to maximum-entropy RL, with practical guidance on choosing algorithms for real-robot deployment.

item.title: Week 9: Exploration, Partial Observability, and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Exploration strategies (count-based, ICM, RND), partial observability via POMDPs and recurrent policies, and multi-agent RL with CTDE — connecting all three to modern agentic AI systems.

item.title: Week 10: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning and Planning
item.description: From Dyna to Dreamer to MuZero — the model-based RL design space: learned world models, receding-horizon MPC, latent-space planning, and how these connect to tree-of-thought reasoning in modern LLMs.

item.title: Week 11: Offline Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Why standard RL fails on fixed datasets — and how conservative Q-learning (CQL), implicit Q-learning (IQL), behavior regularization, and doubly robust off-policy evaluation enable learning from offline data without environment interaction.

item.title: Week 12: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
item.description: RLHF pipeline: supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling via Bradley-Terry preferences, and KL-regularized PPO for aligning language models with human values.

item.title: Week 13: Direct Preference Optimization and GRPO
item.description: DPO eliminates the reward model by inverting the KL-regularized optimal policy; GRPO replaces the value critic with a group-normalized empirical baseline for verifiable reasoning tasks.

item.title: Week 14: Agentic Systems and Course Capstone
item.description: Capstone: map agentic AI architectures (ReAct, Reflexion, plan-and-execute) onto the MDP formalism, covering memory, safety constraints, process rewards, and open problems.

item.title: The Position Update: Gain from Prediction and Measurement
item.description: Where the sensor weight comes from. Prediction uncertainty and sensor spread set the gain, and a 1-D tracking lab shows what a shove does to the estimate.

item.title: Robotics Foundations: Sensors, Actions, and Motion
item.description: The sense → decide → act loop, the parts of a robot arm, and how two joint angles decide where the hand lands — a beginner robotics lesson with a runnable 2-DOF arm lab.

item.title: Week 1: Robot Modeling and Kinematics
item.description: Configuration spaces, forward and inverse kinematics, and the Jacobian — the geometric foundations that map joint angles to end-effector pose in SE(3).

item.title: Robots Under Uncertainty: Estimating Position from Noisy Sensors
item.description: A rover in an aisle blends a prediction with a noisy measurement. One slider is that weight, and the estimate mark is the blend.

item.title: Week 2: Dynamics and State Estimation
item.description: From geometry to forces: rigid-body dynamics and state estimation, including the Kalman and extended Kalman filter for tracking robot state under noise.

item.title: Week 3: Control Fundamentals
item.description: Feedback control for robots — PID, computed-torque, and the trajectory-tracking foundations that turn desired motions into stable actuator commands.

item.title: Week 4: Teleoperation and Data Collection
item.description: How expert demonstration data is gathered — teleoperation interfaces, synchronized state-action logging, and the data-quality choices that determine what a policy can learn.

item.title: Week 5: Imitation Learning
item.description: Learning controllers from demonstration — behavior cloning, its compounding-error failure mode, and the foundations of imitation learning from state-action trajectories.

item.title: Week 6: Reinforcement Learning for Robotics
item.description: Connecting RL theory to physical robots — why imitation alone is insufficient, and how policy-gradient methods let robots improve beyond demonstrated behavior.

item.title: Week 7: Sim2Real Pipelines and IsaacLab
item.description: Bridging the simulation-to-reality gap with domain randomization and the IsaacLab pipeline for training transferable robot policies at scale.

item.title: Week 8: Foundation Models for Manipulation — ACT and Action Chunking
item.description: Why reactive per-timestep policies fail on long-horizon manipulation, and how Action Chunking Transformers (ACT) predict coherent sequences of future actions.

item.title: Week 9: Flow Matching and Diffusion for Robot Policies
item.description: Generative robot policies — diffusion and flow-matching models that sample multimodal action trajectories for dexterous manipulation.

item.title: Week 10: Vision–Language–Action Models
item.description: Vision-Language-Action models that fuse perception, language, and action into a single policy — architecture, training, and how language grounds robot behavior.

item.title: Week 11: Fine-Tuning and Adaptation
item.description: Adapting pretrained VLA models to new robots and tasks — fine-tuning strategies that preserve broad manipulation priors while specializing behavior.

item.title: Week 12: Safety, Constraints, and Reliability
item.description: Formal safety for learned controllers — control barrier functions, constraint enforcement, and reliability guarantees for robots acting near people.

item.title: Week 13: Multi-Robot and Multi-Task Learning
item.description: Scaling beyond a single robot and task — multi-task policy learning and coordination strategies across multiple robots.

item.title: Week 14: Sim2Real Capstone
item.description: A capstone synthesizing modeling, control, imitation, RL, and sim2real into an end-to-end pipeline for training and deploying a real robot policy.

item.title: Week 1: Modern Vision Backbones
item.description: Trace the evolution from convolutional networks to Vision Transformers, formalize self-attention over image patches, and survey native 3D representations (NeRF, Gaussian Splatting) that ground vision models in physical space.

item.title: Week 2: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Vision
item.description: How VLM vision encoders are pretrained without labels — contrastive learning, masked autoencoding (MAE), and self-distillation (DINO), and why each objective yields representations with different geometric properties.

item.title: Week 3: Contrastive Vision–Language Learning (CLIP)
item.description: Derive the CLIP architecture and its symmetric contrastive objective, see how zero-shot classification emerges from vector similarity, and understand the limits that motivated later vision-language models.

item.title: Week 4: Beyond CLIP — Captioning and Grounding
item.description: Move from discriminative to generative perception: encoder-decoder captioning and cross-attention grounding that let models describe what they see and localize where objects are.

item.title: Week 5: BLIP, BLIP-2, and Related Models
item.description: Unify contrastive alignment with generative captioning through BLIP, then meet the Q-Former — the low-parameter bottleneck bridging frozen vision encoders and frozen LLMs without catastrophic forgetting.

item.title: Week 6: LLaVA and Multimodal Instruction Tuning
item.description: Multimodal instruction tuning — how LLaVA's minimalist projector design and supervised instruction-response pairs turn a captioner into a conversational visual assistant.

item.title: Week 7: Alternative VLM Architectures
item.description: Beyond projector-based VLMs: Flamingo's gated cross-attention, the Perceiver's latent bottleneck, PaLI's unified encoder-decoder, and extensions to tactile and non-visual modalities.

item.title: Week 8: Fine-Tuning and Parameter-Efficient Methods
item.description: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning for billion-parameter VLMs — the mathematics of LoRA and QLoRA, memory budgeting, and continuous learning on edge robotics hardware.

item.title: Week 9: Evaluation and Robustness
item.description: Why benchmark accuracy misleads — captioning, VQA, and grounding metrics, distribution shift and spurious correlations, and the adversarial testing needed before physical deployment.

item.title: Week 10: ControlNet and Controlled Generation
item.description: Precise geometric control over diffusion models via ControlNet and zero-initialized convolutions, and how VLMs act as System-2 controllers translating language into structured conditioning signals.

item.title: Week 11: Multimodal Agents and Tool Use
item.description: From passive perception to action — VLMs as the policy engine of a POMDP, grounding language intentions into tool calls and affordances to complete multi-step tasks.

item.title: Week 12: Vision-Language Models for Robotics
item.description: Embodying VLMs in robots: perceiving unstructured environments, interpreting natural-language instructions, and producing continuous motor commands under real-time and safety constraints.

item.title: Week 13: Bias, Fairness, and Safety in VLMs
item.description: How web-scale training imprints systematic representation bias, how text-to-image models amplify stereotypes, and the alignment methods (RLHF, DPO) used to constrain VLM behavior before deployment.

item.title: Week 14: Vision-Language Capstone
item.description: Integrate thirteen weeks of perception, generation, and embodiment into a coherent vision-language system design — architecture, alignment, and safety for a deployed VLM.

item.title: Week 1: Probabilistic Foundations
item.description: The probabilistic vocabulary shared by every generative model — maximum likelihood, latent-variable models, the evidence lower bound, amortized inference, and score functions — and where each model class sits on the expressiveness–tractability frontier.

item.title: Week 2: Variational Autoencoders
item.description: The VAE operationalizes the ELBO — the reparameterization trick, posterior collapse and its mitigations, β-VAE disentanglement, VQ-VAE, and hierarchical variants — the template for every latent-variable generative model.

item.title: Week 3: Generative Adversarial Networks
item.description: The adversarial game and its divergence geometry — the min-max objective and its Jensen-Shannon interpretation, mode collapse and training instability, the Wasserstein reformulation with gradient penalty, spectral normalization, conditional and StyleGAN architectures, and FID/precision/recall evaluation.

item.title: Week 4: Energy-Based Models and Score Matching
item.description: Energy-based models and the partition-function problem — contrastive divergence, Langevin dynamics sampling and the mixing challenge, score matching and denoising score matching, and NCSN multi-scale score estimation as the direct mathematical precursor to diffusion models.

item.title: Week 5: Normalizing Flows
item.description: Exact-likelihood generative modeling through invertible maps — the change-of-variables formula, affine coupling layers (RealNVP, Glow), autoregressive flows and the training/sampling speed duality, continuous normalizing flows via neural ODEs, and the link to Schrödinger bridges and flow matching.

item.title: Week 6: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
item.description: Denoising diffusion from first principles — the fixed Gaussian forward process, the variational bound on the reverse process, the simplified noise-prediction objective, the time-conditioned U-Net, ancestral and accelerated DDIM sampling, and the SDE/ODE unification with score matching.

item.title: Week 7: Flow Matching and Consistency Models
item.description: Generative modeling as regression on a vector field — conditional flow matching, rectified flow and straight-line trajectories, optimal-transport coupling via mini-batch Sinkhorn, stochastic interpolants unifying flow matching and DDPM, and consistency models for single-step generation.

item.title: Week 8: Conditioning and Control
item.description: Steering diffusion generation — classifier and classifier-free guidance, the implicit energy-model view and manifold-departure artifacts, cross-attention for text conditioning and its memory advantage, ControlNet structural conditioning with zero convolutions, and adaptive layer normalization.

item.title: Week 9: Latent Diffusion and Multimodal Generation
item.description: Scaling diffusion to high resolution and beyond images — latent diffusion (Stable Diffusion), text conditioning via cross-attention, the diffusion transformer (DiT), and extensions to audio (CLAP), video (temporal attention, 3D convolutions), and multimodal generation.

item.title: Week 10: Evaluating Generative Models
item.description: How to tell whether a generative model is good — bits-per-dimension, FID and its finite-sample bias, Inception Score, precision/recall, text-to-image faithfulness metrics (TIFA, VQAScore), task-success evaluation for robotics, and Goodhart's-law failure modes.

item.title: Week 11: Representation Learning with Generative Models
item.description: What generative models learn internally — generative vs. contrastive self-supervision, masked autoencoders, diffusion-feature correspondence (DIFT), feature-extraction protocols, and why spatially-detailed generative representations excel at robotics perception and planning.

item.title: Week 12: World Models and Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Generative models as learned simulators — the world-model architecture, the recurrent state-space model (RSSM), Dreamer-style latent imagination for policy optimization, latent-space model predictive control, and the sample-efficiency tradeoffs of model-based vs. model-free RL.

item.title: Week 13: Safety, Misuse, and Alignment
item.description: The dual-use risks of generative models — deepfakes and detection, training-data memorization and extraction, differential privacy (DP-SGD), red-teaming and adversarial robustness, and the RLHF/DPO alignment techniques that steer model behavior.

item.title: Week 14: Generative AI Capstone
item.description: Building and evaluating generative systems with scientific rigor — the generative pipeline as a system, controlled ablations and baselines, scaling laws, multi-dimensional and failure-mode evaluation, deployment engineering, and capstone project tracks.

item.title: Week 1: Probability Spaces and Events
item.description: Build probability from sample spaces, events, and Kolmogorov's axioms, and set up discrete vs continuous models.

item.title: Week 2: Random Variables and Distributions
item.description: Map outcomes to numbers with random variables, and work with PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, and four named distributions.

item.title: Week 3: Expectation, Variance, and Covariance
item.description: Compute expectation, variance, and covariance, and use linearity of expectation without requiring independence.

item.title: Week 4: Conditioning and Independence
item.description: Condition on information, factor joints with the chain rule, and separate independence from conditional independence.

item.title: Week 5: Bayes' Rule and Generative Classification
item.description: Update beliefs with Bayes' rule and make MAP decisions in simple generative classification settings.

item.title: Week 6: Multivariate Gaussians
item.description: Parameterize joint Gaussians with mean and covariance, and compute marginals, conditionals, and whitening transforms.

item.title: Week 7: Laws of Large Numbers and the CLT
item.description: See sample averages concentrate with the LLN and become approximately normal with the central limit theorem.

item.title: Week 8: Point Estimation — Maximum Likelihood
item.description: Form the likelihood, maximize it for Bernoulli and Gaussian models, and connect MLE to empirical risk.

item.title: Week 9: Bayesian Estimation and MAP
item.description: Treat parameters as uncertain, update posteriors, and compare MAP estimates to MLE with conjugate examples.

item.title: Week 10: Bias, Variance, and Uncertainty
item.description: Decompose estimation error into bias and variance, form simple confidence intervals, and use the bootstrap as a computational uncertainty tool.

item.title: Week 11: Information Theory for ML
item.description: Define entropy, cross-entropy, and KL divergence, and connect them to maximum likelihood and classification losses.

item.title: Week 12: Exponential Families (lite)
item.description: See Bernoulli, Gaussian, and categorical models as exponential families with natural parameters and sufficient statistics.

item.title: Week 13: Graphical Models (lite)
item.description: Factor joint distributions with directed and undirected graphs, and read conditional independence from graph structure at a cartoon level.

item.title: Week 14: Capstone — Probabilistic Language of ML
item.description: Map probability tools onto reinforcement learning and generative modeling, and audit common probabilistic modeling mistakes.

item.title: Week 1: Optimality Conditions Revisited
item.description: Elevate intermediate first-order intuition into rigorous stationarity conditions and constraint qualifications that unlock KKT and duality.

item.title: Week 2: Lagrangian Duality in Depth
item.description: Build the Lagrangian dual function, prove weak duality, and state Slater's condition for strong duality.

item.title: Week 3: KKT and Sensitivity
item.description: State the full KKT system, use complementary slackness, and read dual variables as shadow prices.

item.title: Week 4: LP, QP, and Conic Form
item.description: Write linear and quadratic programs in standard form and see second-order cone constraints as a modeling tool.

item.title: Week 5: Semidefinite Programming
item.description: Formulate semidefinite programs, visualise spectrahedra at a high level, and see SDP relaxations for hard combinatorial problems.

item.title: Week 6: Interior-Point Methods
item.description: Follow the central path with log barriers, sketch self-concordance at a practical level, and interpret commercial IPM solvers.

item.title: Week 7: Proximal Methods and ADMM
item.description: Use proximal operators for composite objectives, run ISTA/FISTA, and split structure with ADMM.

item.title: Week 8: Newton and Quasi-Newton
item.description: Derive the Newton step, add damping and line search, and use BFGS/L-BFGS when Hessians are unavailable.

item.title: Week 9: Variance Reduction
item.description: Exploit finite-sum structure with SVRG and SAGA to reduce gradient noise without full-batch cost every step.

item.title: Week 10: Large-Batch and Distributed Training
item.description: Scale minibatches across workers with data-parallel gradients, and separate solid theory from large-batch learning-rate folklore.

item.title: Week 11: Automatic Differentiation
item.description: Contrast forward and reverse mode AD, build vector-Jacobian products on a tiny graph, and cost out reverse mode for deep nets.

item.title: Week 12: Sharpness and SAM
item.description: Define sharpness of minima, connect large-batch geometry, and implement a SAM-style ascent-descent step.

item.title: Week 13: Landscapes and Implicit Bias
item.description: Navigate nonconvex landscapes, saddles, and overparameterisation, and see how GD/SGD prefer particular solutions among many minimisers.

item.title: Week 14: Capstone — Structure Meets Scale
item.description: Diagnose a hard problem and choose either a convex cone reformulation path or a large-scale first/second-order training recipe.
